finding.description: Hardcoded API key embedded directly in source code.
finding.rationale: The secret 'sk-live-4f8a9b2c1d3e4f5a6b7c8d9e0f1a2b3c' is committed in plaintext, exposing it to anyone with repository access and making rotation difficult without a code change.

finding.description: SQL injection vulnerability via unsanitized string concatenation in get_user_by_name.
finding.rationale: User-supplied 'name' is concatenated directly into the SQL query without parameterization or escaping, allowing an attacker to manipulate the query structure and access or modify arbitrary data.

finding.description: SQL injection vulnerability via unsanitized f-string interpolation in get_users_by_ids.
finding.rationale: Each user_id from the comma-split request parameter is interpolated directly into the SQL query without parameterization, allowing an attacker to inject arbitrary SQL through the 'ids' query parameter.

finding.description: Function `get_user` has no corresponding test coverage.
finding.rationale: Untested API endpoints can silently regress; all public API functions should have at least one test.

dependency_reason: The hardcoded API key should be removed before tests are written to avoid tests depending on or exposing the hardcoded secret.; api.py get_user calls get_user_by_name, so the SQL injection in get_user_by_name must be fixed before meaningful tests for get_user can be written.

finding.description: N+1 query pattern: `get_users_by_ids` issues one separate SQL query per user ID instead of a single batched query.
finding.rationale: Each iteration of the loop opens a new query execution round-trip to the database; for N ids this produces N queries, causing latency and connection overhead that grows linearly and could be replaced by a single `WHERE id IN (...)` query.

dependency_reason: The SQL injection fix (replacing the f-string interpolation with a parameterized batched query) subsumes the N+1 fix, so the security rewrite should be done first to avoid redundant changes to the same loop.
